SugarCraft\Focus

FocusRing final class

An immutable focus ring: an ordered set of focusable region ids with a single focused member, plus Tab/Shift-Tab traversal that wraps around.

MethodSummary
static new(): selfAn empty ring with nothing registered or focused.
static of(string ...$ids): selfA ring of the given region ids in traversal order (duplicates dropped, first occurrence wins), focusing the first one.
static ofStrict(string ...$ids): selfA strict variant of of() that throws on duplicate ids instead of silently dropping them. Useful when callers want to enforce uniqueness.
register(string $id): selfRegister a region at the end of the traversal order. A no-op (returns the same ring) if it is already registered. Registering into an empty ring focuses the new region. A newly registered region is always enabled.
unregister(string $id): selfRemove a region. A no-op if it was not registered. If the removed region was focused, focus lands on the nearest ENABLED survivor at or after the vacated slot (wrapping to the first enabled region at the end) — the wall that next() skips must not strand the next keystroke. Only when EVERY survivor is disabled does focus keep the slot (clamped to the new end): the parked state, which the next traversal carries off. Focus otherwise stays on the same region. The disabled flag for the removed id is cleared.
trap(): FocusTrapOpen a modal FocusTrap over this ring; call guarding() then release().
focus(string $id): selfFocus a specific registered, ENABLED region. A no-op if it is not registered, is disabled, or is already focused.
canFocus(string $id): boolWhether focus() would actually MOVE focus to $id: registered, enabled, and not already focused. One bool for all three refusal causes — the same wall focus() respects; pair with has()/isEnabled() when the caller must know WHICH refusal happened.
tryFocus(string $id): ?selfAsk-and-refuse form of focus(): the moved ring when focus relocates, null when it would not (unknown id, disabled id, already focused — an empty ring refuses everything, so it answers null too). focus()'s identity-return and this null are the same fact in two grammars; the shared call keeps them from drifting apart.
focusFirst(): selfFocus the first ENABLED region in traversal order — disabled heads are skipped. A no-op when nothing is enabled, or when focus already sits there.
focusLast(): selfFocus the last ENABLED region in traversal order — disabled tails are skipped. A no-op when nothing is enabled, or when focus already sits there.
reorder(string ...$ids): selfReplace the traversal order while keeping focus on the current region id when it survives the dedupe. Acts as a batch set-replace — ids not previously registered are added; ids missing from the new list are dropped.
next(): selfMove focus to the next enabled region (Tab), wrapping past the end. Disabled regions are skipped. Disabling the focused region does not move focus; it is left in place and the next traversal carries it off — onto the nearest enabled region after it, even when that is the only enabled region left. A no-op (returns the same ring) when focus already sits on the only enabled region, or when no region is enabled.
previous(): selfMove focus to the previous enabled region (Shift-Tab), wrapping past the start. Disabled regions are skipped. Disabling the focused region does not move focus; it is left in place and the next traversal carries it off — onto the nearest enabled region before it, even when that is the only enabled region left. A no-op (returns the same ring) when focus already sits on the only enabled region, or when no region is enabled.
nextOf(string $id): ?stringPure query: the id focus would land on stepping forward from $id, without moving focus. Mirrors next() including its no-op shape — an id with nowhere enabled to go answers with itself: when every region is disabled, or when $id is the sole enabled survivor. A parked, disabled query id with any enabled survivor moves to the nearest one in that direction. null when the id is not registered.
previousOf(string $id): ?stringPure query: the id focus would land on stepping backward from $id, without moving focus. Mirrors previous(); see nextOf().
peekNext(): ?stringWhere next() WOULD land if it were called now, without moving focus: the ring-level sibling of nextOf(), answering about the CURRENT focus. null on an empty ring; a parked focus answers via the nearest enabled region, and a nowhere-to-move focus answers with its own id (next()'s no-op shape — callers compare ===current() to detect "Tab would do nothing").
peekPrevious(): ?stringWhere previous() WOULD land if it were called now. See peekNext() for the shared grammar (empty ring null, parked focus carried to the nearest enabled region, no-op answers the current id).
disable(string $id): selfDisable a region so next()/previous() skip over it. Disabling the currently focused region does not move focus — it is a pure metadata change so disable() never causes surprising focus jumps.
enable(string $id): selfRe-enable a previously disabled region. A no-op if the id is not registered or is already enabled.
isEnabled(string $id): boolTrue when the region is registered and not disabled. False conflates unregistered with disabled — use has() to tell them apart.
enabledIds(): array
disabledIds(): array
enabledCount(): intZero-cost enabled region count (avoids array allocation of enabledIds()).
disabledCount(): intZero-cost disabled region count.
getIterator(): \Traversable
jsonSerialize(): arraySnapshot for session persistence: the ids in traversal order, the focused region (as both an id and a position), and the disabled ids in traversal order. Disabled ids are read from $ids rather than from the keys of the disabled set, because PHP coerces a numeric-string key such as "1" to int(1) — the snapshot must stay a list of strings so restore() can consume it verbatim.
static restore(array $snapshot): selfRebuild a ring from a jsonSerialize() snapshot — the inverse of the persistence format.
static fromJson(string $json): ?selfDecode a JSON snapshot string and rebuild through restore() — the file-reading convenience that keeps callers from hand-assembling the json_decode/is_array guard.
current(): ?stringThe focused region id, or null when the ring is empty.
isFocused(string $id): boolWhether $id is the focused member. CAUTION for painters: focus can legally PARK on a disabled region — disable() never moves an existing focus, and unregister() lands on the vacated slot when every survivor is disabled — so draw a focus accent only when isFocused($id) && isEnabled($id) both hold.
has(string $id): bool
index(): intThe focused position into the REGISTERED ids (disabled regions count too), or -1 when the ring is empty. For "region k of n" among the focusable ones use enabledIndex() with enabledCount(). Answers -1 ONLY when empty: a parked focus still reports its raw slot — the two no-answer grammars differ, enabledIndex() nulls on empty AND parked.
enabledIndex(): ?intThe focused region's 0-based ordinal into enabledIds() — the "k" of "region k of n" for a status line. null when the ring is empty or focus is parked on a disabled region, cases where index() counts every registered region and cannot answer; unlike index()'s -1 (empty only), this null also covers the parked state.
ids(): array
count(): intNumber of registered regions (enabled and disabled); backs count($ring).
isEmpty(): bool
isParked(): boolWhether focus currently sits on a DISABLED region — the ring is non-empty and enabledIndex() has no answer. Focus parks ONLY through disable() on the focused id, or unregister()/restore landing it on an all-disabled survivor. The paint rule and the key-routing guard are one question about the whole ring; naming it here stops every call site from recombining the two accessors and getting the empty case wrong. Per-region paint still pairs isFocused()/isEnabled() — this answers about the FOCUSED region.

FocusTrap final class

An immutable modal focus trap over a FocusRing: opening it captures what the dialog interrupts (the focused id and every enabled id) and disables the background; release() undoes it in the one correct order with no argument, because the trap holds its own base state.

MethodSummary
static new(FocusRing $base): selfOpen a trap over $base: every currently enabled region becomes unreachable.
guarding(string ...$ids): selfRegister the dialog's focusable regions and focus the first.
withRing(FocusRing $ring): selfReplace the trapped ring, e.g. after Tab / Shift-Tab inside the dialog.
ring(): FocusRingThe ring as it stands while trapped (background disabled, dialog ids live).
saved(): ?stringThe id focused when the trap opened, or null on an empty ring.
background(): array
dialog(): array
release(): FocusRingClose the dialog: re-enable background, drop dialog ids, restore focus.
